prize_parts.citation: for credibly identified evidence on how import competition and technology reshape labour demand, wages and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: I keep B032 as a single-part prize to Autor, Hanson and Dorn. I narrow the citation from my round-1 wording, which said 'empirical and conceptual analysis'. The chair asked whether the citation should cover the trade-shock evidence only or also the task and skill-premium framework. I now say evidence only. The credited unit I can attribute cleanly is the local-labour-market, import-exposure design and the adjustment evidence it produced, where all three named people are core authors. The task framework is shared with Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo, who are outside this ballot or already recognised, and with Katz. A citation claiming the whole framework would overstate what these three names can honestly carry. On maturity, the chair asked for specific re-examination evidence. From my own recollection, not verified here, the exposure design has been stress-tested in three ways. Methodologists have examined shift-share inference (for example Adão, Kolesár and Morales on standard errors, and Goldsmith-Pinkham, Sorkin and Swift and Borusyak, Hull and Jaravel on identifying assumptions). The authors have followed worker-level adjustment and persistence in later work. Independent groups have re-estimated the local effects. My understanding is that the qualitative finding of slow local adjustment and concentrated, lasting costs has survived this, while aggregate size and persistence remain debated. I treat that as a recollection to be checked, not an established fact. My configuration has not changed in ballot, names or rank order of preference. What changed is the citation scope. As someone who works on measurement and causal inference in comparative data, I weight identification credibility and attribution cleanliness first, then breadth of consequence, then overlap with recent prizes. B032 does best on the first two. I do not count first-place tallies, and no position is near six votes.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still attribution and scope. A trade-shock-only citation leaves out Katz, whose skill-premium and education-technology work is foundational, and it leaves the task framework to people the Committee cannot credit here. Dorn versus Katz remains a close judgement. The magnitude and long-run persistence of the China shock are still contested, and shift-share inference has needed correction, which I read as a sign of scrutiny but which also limits how strongly effects can be stated. Thematic proximity to the 2024 prize and to Card, Angrist and Imbens (2021) and Goldin (2023) could lead some members to see labour and technology as already well recognised. I do not think that overlap is serious, because the trade-shock designs address a different question, but it is a real judgement. A Committee that puts a tight two-person theoretical credit line first, as in B042, has a defensible case.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson prefers Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She frames the citation around technology and trade shocks with the China-shock evidence as the identified core, and she acknowledges that excluding Katz is a real cost. She notes that Katz's skill-premium work sits close to the 2023 prize on which Goldin was a Katz co-author.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and have tightened my wording to match hers. I dropped 'conceptual analysis' so the citation does not claim the task theory. I weigh the Katz exclusion as a real cost too, and I am not fully comfortable with it. I differ slightly on the Goldin proximity. Goldin's prize concerned gender gaps and long-run labour-market history, so I treat it as a reason for modest caution about Katz, not as a reason to exclude him. The decisive reason for Dorn over Katz is that the credited achievement is the local-labour-market design, in which Dorn is a core author and Katz is not.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg ranks B032 first for transparent designs, replication and re-examination. She notes that the aggregate magnitude and the inference properties of exposure designs are contested. She holds cross-country observational evidence to a stricter standard than local quasi-experimental designs, and she keeps B016 off her alternatives list.
responses.response: I share both the reasoning and the standard. The chair asked for specific re-examination evidence. I can only offer recollection, namely the shift-share inference and identification literature and the authors' own later work on persistence. I cannot confirm those results here, and you say you also have incomplete knowledge of the latest re-examinations. Neither of us should overstate maturity. I would phrase it as design credibility that has withstood scrutiny while magnitudes remain open. On B016, the cross-country standard is one I apply from my own work on democratisation, where endogeneity and measurement problems are acute. Unlike you, I keep B016 as an alternative, because the formal framework and later sharper designs are real strengths. I regard that as an honest difference, not a conflict between us.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B014 with Calvo, Taylor and Woodford. He treats the post-2021 inflation episode as a test of empirical performance and not of the contribution, calls the timing mature and arguably overdue, and acknowledges that Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets have strong claims.
responses.response: I accept that B014 passes the criteria on originality, durability and practical consequence, and my round-1 exclusion reflected attribution difficulty, not merit. His point that the three building blocks have identifiable originating work is the strongest attribution argument available for a crowded field. It is stronger than I allowed in round 1. I still cannot treat it as settled, because he concedes that the Committee has to decide between honouring the theoretical originators and the estimated-model strand. That decision changes the names, which makes the credit more contestable than in B032, where the three names are co-authors of one empirical programme. I would not oppose B014 on scientific grounds. If the Committee settles that choice, B014 is the strongest rival to my configuration on breadth of consequence.

responses.point: Friberg prefers Persson, Tabellini and Besley. He argues that the attribution is tidy because the contributions come from long partnerships. He concedes that the cross-country evidence is uneven, that the 2024 prize is adjacent, and that Besley is the most contestable name. He treats B032 as the most serious competing case and would keep Dorn over Katz.
responses.response: We agree on Dorn over Katz. On B016 I accept the formal framework and the later sharper designs as real strengths, which is why it is my second alternative. Two points keep me from ranking it first. As I explain in the conflict note, my own field is adjacent and I am wary of counting my familiarity as merit. I also hold the cross-country identification caveat strictly, and your reply rests the case on the formal framework more than on the cross-country regressions. That is a reasonable argument, but it makes the achievement more of a theoretical programme than B032's evidence is. I read the 2024 overlap as partial. The tidiness of the credit line is a fair point, but a two-person Persson-Tabellini award would be tidier still, as you concede.

responses.point: Enflo prefers B010 with Melitz and Helpman. She treats B032 as a strong alternative whose cleanest credit line is the trade-shock evidence for Autor, Hanson and Dorn, and she says the Katz-inclusive version proposed by Hjalmarsson and Teorell needs explicit discussion. She cautions that the task framework owes much to Acemoglu and Restrepo.
responses.response: Your reading of the cleanest credit line is now my own, and I have moved off my Katz-inclusive round-1 version, so that discussion is resolved on my side. I ranked B010 sixth in my opening, and I do not think I weighed it fairly against the cleanliness of its credit. Two names with a precisely identified core is a real advantage. My remaining hesitation is about evidence. The welfare-gains magnitudes depend on functional form, and the uncredited Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum lineage is a genuine gap. If the Committee accepts a mechanism-only citation, B010 is a defensible choice, but I do not move to it. I keep B032 because its core findings can be checked more directly against data.

responses.point: Hassler prefers B016. He ranks B042 second, calls its attribution cleaner than B016's, and says it would be the natural second path if the Committee weights attribution cleanliness over breadth. His reservations about B042 are that the mechanism rests mostly on theory and calibration, and that the collateral channel is only mixed-identified.
responses.response: I agree that B042's two-person attribution is the cleanest on the list, and I remain convinced of the mechanism's foundational role. That is why B042 is my first alternative and was my opening first choice. Your reservation about identification of the collateral channel is the one I moved on, and I now weight it more heavily. I do not think breadth beats attribution in a general way. The two criteria point in different directions across candidates, and they should be weighed together with identification credibility. B042 leads on attribution, B032 on identification, and B016 on breadth. On the 2022 overlap, I read it as partial. It concerned bank runs and intermediation, not collateral-constraint amplification, but I cannot resolve that from the materials here.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee reads the task framework and the trade-shock evidence as one achievement or two. If it insists on the task framework, Katz's claim strengthens and the attribution problem outside the ballot (Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu, Restrepo) grows, which would push me toward B042.
Dorn versus Katz remains a close call. My choice rests on the local-labour-market design, not on the importance of the skill-premium literature.

My account of the shift-share inference and persistence literature is from recollection and has not been verified. If later re-examination showed that the core local effects do not survive alternative inference, I would withdraw my maturity argument.
Whether the 2024 prize and recent labour-market prizes make B032 less timely than B042 or B014 once the Committee weighs overlap.
Whether the Committee prefers B014 once it settles the originators-versus-estimation question, since B014 is my strongest rival on breadth of consequence.

Prior-prize facts such as the 2022 and 2024 awards and Gertler's status are members' recollections and have not been independently verified here. My judgements rest on my own reading of the literature.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent for B032 from the supplied profile. It documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Hanson, Dorn or Katz. My field (comparative democratisation, quality of government, V-Dem) is adjacent to B016, which I list as an alternative. My 2024 presentation speech concerned institutions and prosperity, but it may reflect collective drafting and does not establish a personal prize preference. The profile documents no collaboration with Persson, Tabellini or Besley, and Hassler's round-1 file only mentions a possible, unverified IIES connection with Persson. At Stockholm University I am a colleague, in a different department, of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart, who is relevant mainly to B014 and B016. This is disclosed and I did not rely on it. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
